source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, adhyaya 2 (the measure of an akshauhini, told right after Samantapanchaka)

figures.note: Adi Parva 2: a patti (1 chariot, 1 elephant, 3 horses, 5 foot) ×3 senamukha ×3 gulma ×3 gana ×3 vahini ×3 pritana ×3 chamu ×3 anikini ×10 akshauhini. The narration rounds the horses and men; the numerals show the exact figures.

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice, used by the timeline), say (what is spoken, if not `text`): '…' and '—' pause, ',' and '.' pause a little, [p:400] pauses 400 ms, {s:0.8} speaks what follows at 0.8× until the next {s:…} ({s} resets).

lines.speaker: elder_sage
lines.text: And what is an akshauhini, the army you speak of?
lines.note: beats[0] = 'akshauhini': the elder leans in and his hand opens toward Sauti

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Listen. One chariot, one elephant, three horses, five soldiers on foot… that is a patti.
lines.note: beats = 'chariot', 'elephant', 'horses', 'soldiers' (each unit steps into the fire-lit frieze), 'patti' (the frieze is framed and named)
the patti shrinks into one block, then copies of the block triple it, again and again (the steps are spread from beats[0] to the next line's 'akshauhini')

lines.text: …until one akshauhini stands: twenty-one thousand, eight hundred and seventy chariots.
lines.note: beats = 'akshauhini' (×10: the last step; its name in gold), 'twenty-one' (the chariot counter reaches 21,870), 'chariots'

lines.text: As many elephants. Sixty-five thousand horses. A hundred and nine thousand soldiers on foot.
lines.note: beats = the elephant row (21,870), the horse row (65,610), the foot-soldier row (109,350): each frieze row slides in and its gold counter rolls up

lines.text: Eighteen such armies gathered on that field.
lines.note: ticks = the 18 army blocks slide into place (11 Kaurava, then 7 Pandava); a conch on beats[0] and on beats[1] ('field')

lines.text: And for eighteen days… they fought.
lines.say: And for eighteen days… [p:700] they fought.
lines.note: ticks = 18 days: day/night flickers, a tally mark cut for each (from 'days' to near the line's end, through the hold); beats = 'eighteen', 'fought'
spoken over the end card, which shows strings.episodeLabel / episodeTitle instead of a caption
